title.zh: 卷一百〇二 列傳第四十: 僕散安貞 田琢 完顏弼 蒙古綱 必蘭阿魯帶
title.en: Volume 102 Biographies 40: Pusa Nanzhen, Tian Zuo, Wan Yanbi, Meng Gugang, Bilanaludai
title.raw: 卷一百〇二 列傳第四十: 僕散安貞 田琢 完顏弼 蒙古綱 必蘭阿魯帶 Volume 102 Biographies 40: Pusa Nanzhen, Tian Zuo, Wan Yanbi, Meng Gugang, Bilanaludai

sentences.zh: 僕散安貞

translations.literal: Pusan Anzhen
translations.idiomatic: Pusan Anzhen

sentences.zh: 僕散安貞，本名阿海，以大臣子充奉禦。

translations.literal: Pusan Anzhen, original name Ahai, served as a palace attendant by virtue of being a minister's son.
translations.idiomatic: Pusan Anzhen, whose original name was Ahai, entered court service as a palace attendant because his father was a high minister.

sentences.zh: 父揆，尚韓國公主，鄭王永蹈同母妹也。

translations.literal: His father Kui married the Princess of Han, who was a uterine sister of Prince Yong of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kui had married a princess of Han—a half-sister of Prince Yongdao of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 永蹈誅，安貞罷歸，召為符寶祗候。

translations.literal: When Yongdao was executed, Anzhen was dismissed and sent home, then recalled as a talisman attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongdao was put to death, Anzhen was removed from office and sent home, then recalled as a keeper of the imperial talismans.

sentences.zh: 複為奉禦，尚邢國長公主，加駙馬都尉，襲胡王愛割蠻猛安。

translations.literal: He again became a palace attendant, married the eldest princess of Xing, was made Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant, and inherited the Huwang Aige Manmeng'an fief.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to palace attendance, married the eldest princess of Xing, received the title Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant, and inherited the Huwang Aige Manmeng'an domain.

sentences.zh: 曆尚衣直長、禦院通進、尚藥副使。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Director of the Wardrobe Bureau, Imperial Pantry Commissioner, and Vice Commissioner of the Imperial Pharmacy.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as director of the wardrobe bureau, commissioner of the imperial pantry, and vice commissioner of the imperial pharmacy.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起複，轉符寶郎，除同知定海軍節度使事。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he observed mourning, then was recalled from mourning, transferred to Talisman Attendant, and appointed Acting Military Commissioner of Dinghai Army.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he went into mourning, was soon recalled to duty, became a talisman attendant, and was named acting military commissioner of the Dinghai army.

sentences.zh: 曆邳、淄、涿州刺史，拱衛直都指揮使。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Pi, Zi, and Zhuo, and as Commander of the Archery Guard Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: He held the prefectures of Pi, Zi, and Zhuo in succession and commanded the archery guard directorate.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，改右副點檢兼侍衛親軍副都指揮使，遷元帥左都監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou he was changed to Right Deputy Inspector concurrent Vice Commander of the Palace Guard, and promoted to Left Overseer of the Marshalate.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyou era he became right deputy inspector and vice commander of the palace guard, then was promoted to left overseer of the marshalate.

sentences.zh: 二年，中都解嚴，河北州郡未破者惟真定、大名、東平、清、沃、徐、邳、海州而已。

translations.literal: In the second year the capital lifted its emergency curfew; among Hebei prefectures and districts still unbroken were only Zhending, Daming, Dongping, Qing, Wo, Xu, Pi, and Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the capital ended martial law; in Hebei only Zhending, Daming, Dongping, Qing, Wo, Xu, Pi, and Haizhou still held out.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣安貞與兵部尚書裴滿子仁、刑部尚書武都分道宣撫。

translations.literal: The court sent Anzhen with Minister of War Peiman Ziren and Minister of Justice Wudu to tour and pacify by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: The court dispatched Anzhen, together with Minister of War Peiman Ziren and Minister of Justice Wudu, to conduct pacification tours along separate routes.

sentences.zh: 於是除安貞山東路統軍安撫等使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Anzhen was appointed Military Commissioner and Pacification Commissioner of the Shandong Circuit and related offices.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhen was then made military commissioner and pacification commissioner for the Shandong circuit.

sentences.zh: 初，益都縣人楊安國自少無賴，以鬻鞍材為業，市人呼為「楊鞍兒」，遂自名楊安兒。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yang Anguo of Yidu County had been a wastrel from youth; he made his living selling saddle materials, and market folk called him "Yang the Saddle-Seller," whereupon he styled himself Yang An'er.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a Yidu man named Yang Anguo had been a wastrel since boyhood. He sold saddle fittings for a living; townspeople nicknamed him "Yang the Saddle-Seller," and he took the name Yang An'er.

sentences.zh: 泰和伐宋，山東無賴往往相聚剽掠，詔州郡招捕之。

translations.literal: During the Taihe campaign against Song, ruffians in Shandong often banded together to plunder; an edict ordered prefectures and districts to recruit and capture them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe war against Song, Shandong ruffians often banded together to raid, and the throne ordered local governments to recruit them or hunt them down.

sentences.zh: 安兒降，隸諸軍，累官刺史、防禦使。

translations.literal: An'er surrendered, was attached to the armies, and rose through the ranks to prefect and defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: An'er submitted, entered army service, and eventually rose to prefect and defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 大安三年，招鐵瓦敢戰軍，得千餘人，以唐括合打為都統，安兒為副統，戍邊。

translations.literal: In the third year of Da'an he recruited the Iron-Tile Dare-to-Fight Army, obtaining more than a thousand men; Tangguo Heda was made commander, An'er deputy commander, to garrison the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In Da'an year three he raised the Iron-Tile Dare-to-Fight Army—over a thousand men—with Tangguo Heda as commander and An'er as deputy, and sent them to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 至雞鳴山不進。

translations.literal: They reached Jiming Mountain and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: They halted at Jiming Mountain and refused to advance.

sentences.zh: 衛紹王驛召問狀，安兒乃曰：「平章參政軍數十萬在前，無可慮者。

translations.literal: Prince Shao of Wei summoned him by post-station relay to inquire; An'er then said, "The Grand Councillors and Participation Councillors have several hundred thousand troops ahead—there is nothing to worry about.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shao of Wei summoned him by courier to explain the situation. An'er said, "The grand councillors and participation councillors have hundreds of thousands of men in the van—there is nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 屯駐雞鳴山，所以備間道透漏者耳。」

translations.literal: Stationing at Jiming Mountain is only to guard against enemy penetration by side paths."
translations.idiomatic: We are camped at Jiming Mountain only to block side routes the enemy might slip through."

sentences.zh: 朝廷信其言。

translations.literal: The court believed his words.
translations.idiomatic: The court believed him.

sentences.zh: 安兒乃亡歸山東，與張汝楫聚黨攻劫州縣，殺略官吏，山東大擾。

translations.literal: An'er then fled back to Shandong, gathered a band with Zhang Ruji to attack and plunder prefectures and districts, kill and rob officials, and threw Shandong into great turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: An'er then fled back to Shandong, joined Zhang Ruji in raiding counties and prefectures, killing officials and looting wherever they went, until all Shandong was in uproar.

sentences.zh: 安貞至益都，敗安兒於城東。

translations.literal: Anzhen reached Yidu and defeated An'er east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Anzhen reached Yidu he routed An'er east of the walls.

sentences.zh: 安兒奔萊陽。

translations.literal: An'er fled to Laiyang.
translations.idiomatic: An'er fled toward Laiyang.

sentences.zh: 萊州徐汝賢以城降安兒，賊勢複振。

translations.literal: Xu Ruxian of Laizhou surrendered the city to An'er, and the rebels' strength revived.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ruxian of Laizhou handed the city to An'er, and rebel strength surged again.

sentences.zh: 登州刺史耿格開門納偽鄒都統，以州印付之，郊迎安兒，發帑藏以勞賊。

translations.literal: Geng Ge, prefect of Dengzhou, opened the gates to admit the false Zou commander-in-chief, handed over the prefectural seal, went out to the suburbs to welcome An'er, and opened the treasury to reward the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Ge, prefect of Dengzhou, opened his gates to a rebel commander styling himself commander of Zou, surrendered the prefectural seal, went out to welcome An'er in the suburbs, and emptied the treasury to reward the band.

sentences.zh: 安兒遂僭號，置官屬，改元天順，凡符印詔表儀式皆格草定，遂陷寧海，攻濰州。

translations.literal: An'er then usurped a reign title, established officials, changed the era name to Tianshun; Geng Ge drafted all seals, edicts, memorials, and ceremonial forms, then seized Ninghai and attacked Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: An'er declared himself ruler, set up a court, adopted the era name Tianshun, and had Geng Ge draft every seal, edict, and ritual form; he then took Ninghai and besieged Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 偽元帥方郭三據密州，略沂、海。

translations.literal: The false marshal Fang Guo San held Mizhou and raided Yi and Hai.
translations.idiomatic: A rebel marshal called Fang Guo San held Mizhou and raided the Yi and Hai regions.

sentences.zh: 李全略臨朐，扼穆陵關，欲取益都。

translations.literal: Li Quan raided Linqu, seized Muling Pass, and intended to take Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Quan struck at Linqu, seized Muling Pass, and aimed to take Yidu.

sentences.zh: 安貞以沂州防禦使僕散留家為左翼，安化軍節度使完顏訛論為右翼。

translations.literal: Anzhen made Defense Commissioner of Yizhou Pusan Liujia his left wing and Military Commissioner of Anhua Army Wanyan Elun his right wing.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhen placed Yizhou defense commissioner Pusan Liujia on his left and Anhua army commissioner Wanyan Elun on his right.

sentences.zh: 七月庚辰，安貞軍昌邑東，徐汝賢等以三州之眾十萬來拒戰。

translations.literal: On gengchen of the seventh month Anzhen's army was east of Changyi; Xu Ruxian and others brought a hundred thousand men from three prefectures to resist.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh month's gengchen day Anzhen camped east of Changyi; Xu Ruxian and others marched a hundred thousand men from three prefectures to meet him.

sentences.zh: 自午抵暮，轉戰三十裏，殺賊數萬，獲器械不可勝計。

translations.literal: From noon until evening they fought for thirty li, killing tens of thousands of rebels and capturing weapons beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: From noon to dusk the battle rolled thirty li; tens of thousands of rebels were killed and captured arms piled beyond count.

sentences.zh: 壬午，賊棘七率眾四萬陣于辛河。

translations.literal: On renwu the rebel Ji Qi led forty thousand men and formed battle lines on the Xin River.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu the rebel Ji Qi drew up forty thousand men along the Xin River.

sentences.zh: 安貞令留家由上流膠西濟，繼以大兵，殺獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Anzhen ordered Liujia to cross upstream at Jiaoxi, then followed with the main force; kills and captures were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhen sent Liujia across upstream at Jiaoxi, then brought up the main army; the slaughter and captures were immense.

sentences.zh: 甲申，安貞軍至萊州，偽甯海州刺史史潑立以二十萬陣於城東。

translations.literal: On jiashen Anzhen's army reached Laizhou; the false Ninghai prefect Shi Poli arrayed two hundred thousand east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Anzhen reached Laizhou, where the rebel prefect of Ninghai, Shi Poli, lined up two hundred thousand men east of the walls.

sentences.zh: 留家先以輕兵薄賊，諸將繼之，賊大敗，殺獲且半，以重賞招之，不應。

translations.literal: Liujia first pressed the rebels with light troops; the generals followed; the rebels were utterly defeated, and kills and captures amounted to half their force; heavy rewards were offered to induce surrender, but they did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Liujia probed with light troops, the other commanders closed in, and the rebels were shattered—roughly half killed or captured. Heavy bribes were offered for surrender; none accepted.

sentences.zh: 安貞遣萊州黥卒曹全、張德、田貴、宋福詐降于徐汝賢以為內應。

translations.literal: Anzhen sent the tattooed convicts of Laizhou—Cao Quan, Zhang De, Tian Gui, and Song Fu—to feign surrender to Xu Ruxian as inside collaborators.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhen sent four tattooed convicts of Laizhou—Cao Quan, Zhang De, Tian Gui, and Song Fu—to feign defection to Xu Ruxian as inside men.

sentences.zh: 全與賊西南隅戍卒姚雲相結，約納官軍。

translations.literal: Quan joined with the rebel garrison soldier Yao Yun at the southwest corner and agreed to admit the government army.
translations.idiomatic: Quan won over a rebel sentry named Yao Yun at the southwest corner and agreed to let government troops in.

sentences.zh: 丁亥夜，全縋城出，潛告留家。

translations.literal: On the night of dinghai Quan let himself down from the wall and secretly informed Liujia.
translations.idiomatic: That dinghai night Quan slipped over the wall on a rope and secretly told Liujia.

sentences.zh: 留家募勇敢士三十人從全入城，姚雲納之，大軍畢登，遂複萊州，斬徐汝賢及諸賊將以徇。

translations.literal: Liujia recruited thirty brave men to enter the city with Quan; Yao Yun admitted them; the main army all scaled the walls, recovered Laizhou, and beheaded Xu Ruxian and the rebel generals as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Liujia picked thirty bold men to follow Quan inside; Yao Yun let them in; the main force swarmed over the walls, retook Laizhou, and beheaded Xu Ruxian and the rebel commanders as a warning.

sentences.zh: 安兒脫身走，訛論以兵追之。

translations.literal: An'er escaped; Elun pursued with troops.
translations.idiomatic: An'er slipped away, but Elun pursued with troops.

sentences.zh: 耿格、史潑立皆降。

translations.literal: Geng Ge and Shi Poli both surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Ge and Shi Poli both submitted.

sentences.zh: 留家略定膠西諸縣，宣差伯德玩襲殺方郭三，複密州。

translations.literal: Liujia pacified the counties of Jiaoxi; Commissioner Bode Wan ambushed and killed Fang Guo San and recovered Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liujia secured the Jiaoxi counties; commissioner Bode Wan ambushed and killed Fang Guo San and retook Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 余賊在諸州者皆潰去。

translations.literal: The remaining rebels in the various prefectures all scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel bands still holding other prefectures broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 安兒嘗遣梁居實、黃縣甘泉鎮監酒石抹充浮海赴遼東構留哥，已具舟，皆捕斬之。

translations.literal: An'er had once sent Liang Jushi and the Ganquan Town wine supervisor Shimochong of Huang County to cross the sea to Liaodong to intrigue with Liuge; boats were already prepared—all were captured and executed.
translations.idiomatic: An'er had once sent Liang Jushi and the Ganquan town wine inspector Shimochong of Huang County by sea to Liaodong to treat with Liuge; their boats were ready when all were seized and executed.

sentences.zh: 十一月戊辰，曲赦山東，除楊安兒、耿格及諸故官家作過驅奴不赦外，劉二祖、張汝楫、李思溫及應脅誘從賊，並在本路自為寇盜，罪無輕重，並與赦免。

translations.literal: On wuchen of the eleventh month a partial amnesty was issued for Shandong; except for Yang An'er, Geng Ge, and former officials' runaway bond-servants who had committed crimes—all unpardoned—Liu Erzu, Zhang Ruji, Li Siwen, and those coerced or enticed to follow the rebels, as well as those who had become bandits on their own within the circuit, regardless of the severity of guilt, were all pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: On the eleventh month's wuchen day Shandong received a limited amnesty: Yang An'er, Geng Ge, and runaway bond-servants of former officials were excluded, but Liu Erzu, Zhang Ruji, Li Siwen, coerced followers, and anyone who had turned bandit within the circuit—whatever the crime—were all forgiven.

sentences.zh: 獲楊安兒者，官職俱授三品，賞錢十萬貫。

translations.literal: Whoever captured Yang An'er would be granted a third-rank office and a reward of one hundred thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: Whoever captured Yang An'er would receive a third-rank post and a reward of one hundred thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 十二月辛亥，耿格伏誅，妻子皆遠徙。

translations.literal: On xinhai of the twelfth month Geng Ge was executed; his wife and children were all exiled far away.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth month's xinhai day Geng Ge was executed and his family exiled.

sentences.zh: 諸軍方攻大沫堌，赦至，宣撫副使、知東平府事烏林答與即引軍還。

translations.literal: The armies were attacking Damogu when the amnesty arrived; Pacification Vice Commissioner and Acting Prefect of Dongping Wulindaxi Yu immediately withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Government forces were besieging Damogu when the amnesty arrived; pacification vice commissioner and acting prefect of Dongping Wulindaxi Yu at once withdrew.

sentences.zh: 賊眾乘之，複出為患。

translations.literal: The rebel masses seized the opportunity and came out again to cause trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels seized the chance and broke out again.

sentences.zh: 詔以陝西統軍使完顏弼知東平府事，權宣撫副使。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Shaanxi Military Commissioner Wanyan Bi to know the affairs of Dongping Prefecture and act as Pacification Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The throne named Shaanxi military commissioner Wanyan Bi prefect of Dongping and acting pacification vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 其後楊安兒與汲政等乘舟入海，欲走岠嵎山。

translations.literal: Afterward Yang An'er with Ji Zheng and others took boats to sea, intending to flee to Juyu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yang An'er, Ji Zheng, and others put to sea, aiming to reach Juyu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 舟人曲成等擊之，墜水死。

translations.literal: The boatmen Qu Cheng and others attacked them; he fell into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Boatmen led by Qu Cheng attacked them; An'er fell overboard and drowned.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，安貞遣提控紇石烈牙吾塔破巨蒙等四堌，及破馬耳山，殺劉二祖賊四千餘人，降餘黨八千，擒偽宣差程寬、招軍大使程福，招降脅從百姓三萬余人。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year Anzhen sent Commander Hesilie Yayuta to break the four stockades including Jumeng and to break Ma'er Mountain, killing more than four thousand of Liu Erzu's rebels, accepting the surrender of eight thousand remaining partisans, capturing the false Commissioner Cheng Kuan and Recruitment Envoy Cheng Fu, and inducing more than thirty thousand coerced commoners to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, second month, Anzhen sent commander Hesilie Yayuta to storm four stockades including Jumeng and Ma'er Mountain, killing over four thousand of Liu Erzu's men, accepting eight thousand surrenders, seizing the rebel commissioners Cheng Kuan and Cheng Fu, and winning back more than thirty thousand coerced civilians.

sentences.zh: 安貞遣兵會宿州提控夾谷石裏哥同攻大沫堌，賊千余逆戰。

translations.literal: Anzhen sent troops to join Suzhou Commander Jiagu Shilige in attacking Damogu; more than a thousand rebels met them in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhen joined Suzhou commander Jiagu Shilige in assaulting Damogu; over a thousand rebels met them.

sentences.zh: 石裏哥，以騎兵擊之，盡殪。

translations.literal: Shilige struck them with cavalry and annihilated them all.
translations.idiomatic: Shilige charged with cavalry and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 提控沒烈奪其北門以入，別軍取賊水寨，諸軍繼進，殺賊五千餘人。

translations.literal: Commander Molie seized the north gate to enter; a separate force took the rebel water camp; the armies followed in and killed more than five thousand rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Molie forced the north gate; another column took the rebel river camp; the main forces followed and killed more than five thousand.

sentences.zh: 劉二祖被創，獲之，及偽參謀官崔天佑，楊安兒偽太師李思溫。

translations.literal: Liu Erzu was wounded and captured, along with the false staff officer Cui Tianyou and Yang An'er's false Grand Preceptor Li Siwen.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Erzu was wounded and taken, together with the rebel staff officer Cui Tianyou and Yang An'er's false grand preceptor Li Siwen.

sentences.zh: 餘眾保大小峻角子山，前後追擊，殺獲以萬計，斬劉二祖。

translations.literal: The remainder held the Greater and Lesser Junjiaozi Mountains; pursued repeatedly, kills and captures numbered in the tens of thousands, and Liu Erzu was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors held out on the Greater and Lesser Junjiaozi mountains; repeated pursuits killed and captured by the tens of thousands, and Liu Erzu was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 詔遷賞沒烈等有差。

translations.literal: An edict ordered promotions and rewards for Molie and others according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: Molie and the others were promoted and rewarded according to merit.

sentences.zh: 詔尚書省曰：「山東東、西路賊黨猶嘯聚作過者，詔書到日，並與免罪，各令複業。

translations.literal: An edict to the Masters of Writing said: "Among rebel bands in the eastern and western Shandong circuits who still gather and commit crimes, on the day the edict arrives all are to be pardoned and each ordered to resume his livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: An edict to the Masters of Writing Bureau said: "Rebel bands still active in eastern and western Shandong are pardoned from the day this edict arrives and told to return to their trades.

sentences.zh: 在處官司盡心招撫，優加存恤，無令失所。」

translations.literal: Officials everywhere are to recruit and pacify them with full effort, treat them generously and with care, and not let them lose their homes."
translations.idiomatic: Local officials must recruit them in earnest, treat them generously, and see that none are left destitute."

sentences.zh: 十月，安貞遷樞密副使，行院於徐州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Anzhen was transferred to Vice Director of the Privy Council and established his field headquarters at Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Anzhen became vice director of the privy council and set up his field headquarters at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，楊安兒餘黨複擾山東。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year the remnants of Yang An'er again disturbed Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, second month, Yang An'er's remnants again ravaged Shandong.

sentences.zh: 詔安貞與蒙古綱、完顏弼以近詔招之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Anzhen, Meng Gugang, and Wanyan Bi to recruit them under the recent edict.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhen, Meng Gugang, and Wanyan Bi were ordered to offer amnesty under the recent edict.

sentences.zh: 五月，安貞遣兵討郝定，連戰皆克，殺九萬人，降者三萬余，郝定僅以身免。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Anzhen sent troops to suppress Hao Ding; battle after battle was won, ninety thousand were killed, more than thirty thousand surrendered, and Hao Ding barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Anzhen campaigned against Hao Ding, winning every engagement: ninety thousand killed, more than thirty thousand surrendered, while Hao Ding alone escaped.

sentences.zh: 獲偽金銀牌、器械甚眾，來歸且萬人，皆安慰複業。

translations.literal: Many false gold and silver tallies and weapons were captured; nearly ten thousand came over and were all comforted and restored to their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Great stores of false tallies and arms were taken; nearly ten thousand defectors were settled back into civilian life.

sentences.zh: 自楊安兒、劉二祖敗後，河北殘破，干戈相尋。

translations.literal: After the defeats of Yang An'er and Liu Erzu, Hebei lay in ruins and warfare followed one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang An'er and Liu Erzu fell, Hebei was shattered and war followed war.

sentences.zh: 其黨往往復相團結，所在寇掠，皆衣紅納襖以相識別，號「紅襖賊」。

translations.literal: Their partisans often banded together again, plundering wherever they were; all wore red lined jackets to recognize one another and were called the "Red-Jacket Bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Their followers regrouped everywhere, raiding in red lined jackets that marked them as the "Red-Jacket Bandits."

sentences.zh: 官軍雖討之，不能除也。

translations.literal: Although government troops campaigned against them, they could not be eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: Government armies hunted them, yet could not root them out.

sentences.zh: 大概皆李全、國用安、時青之徒焉。

translations.literal: For the most part they were men of the type of Li Quan, Guo Yong'an, and Shi Qing.
translations.idiomatic: For the most part they were men like Li Quan, Guo Yong'an, and Shi Qing.

sentences.zh: 五年，複伐宋。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Song campaign was resumed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Jin again attacked Song.

sentences.zh: 二月，安貞出息州，軍於七裏鎮，宋兵據淨居山，遣兵擊敗之。

translations.literal: In the second month Anzhen marched out from Xizhou and encamped at Qili Town; Song troops held Jingju Mountain; he sent troops and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Anzhen marched from Xizhou to Qili Town; Song held Jingju Mountain until he sent troops and broke them.

sentences.zh: 宋兵保山寺。

translations.literal: The Song troops defended themselves in the mountain temple.
translations.idiomatic: The Song force fell back into a mountain temple.

sentences.zh: 縱火焚寺，乘勝追至洪門山。

translations.literal: He set fire and burned the temple, then pursued in victory to Hongmen Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He burned the temple and pressed the pursuit to Hongmen Mountain.

sentences.zh: 宋兵方浚濠立柵，安貞軍亟戰，奪其柵。

translations.literal: The Song troops were digging moats and erecting palisades; Anzhen's army fought swiftly and seized their palisades.
translations.idiomatic: While Song was digging moats and raising palisades, Anzhen attacked at once and took their works.

sentences.zh: 宋黃統制團兵五千保黃土關，關絕險，素有備，堅壁不出。

translations.literal: Song Commander Huang's regiment of five thousand held Huangtu Pass; the pass was extremely perilous, long prepared, and they held the walls and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Five thousand Song troops under Commander Huang held Huangtu Pass—a formidable, well-provisioned strongpoint—and refused to sally.

sentences.zh: 安貞遣輕兵分為左右軍潛登，別以兵三千直逼關門。

translations.literal: Anzhen sent light troops divided into left and right wings to climb secretly, and separately sent three thousand men straight against the pass gate.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhen sent light troops up both flanks by stealth and three thousand more straight at the gate.

sentences.zh: 翼日，左右軍會於山顛，俯瞰關內。

translations.literal: The next day the left and right wings met on the mountain crest and looked down into the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Next day both wings met on the ridge and looked down into the pass.

sentences.zh: 宋人守關者望之，駭𥈭不能立。

translations.literal: The Song defenders of the pass saw them and were so terrified they could not stand.
translations.idiomatic: The Song garrison saw them and were too stunned to hold their ground.

sentences.zh: 中軍急攻，宋兵潰，遂奪黃土關。

translations.literal: The center army attacked swiftly; the Song troops collapsed, and Huangtu Pass was taken.
translations.idiomatic: The center struck hard; Song broke, and Huangtu Pass fell.

sentences.zh: 遂入梅林關，拔麻城縣，抵大江，至黃州，克之。

translations.literal: He then entered Meilin Pass, took Macheng County, reached the Great River, arrived at Huangzhou, and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed through Meilin Pass, took Macheng, reached the Yangzi, and captured Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 進克蘄州，前後殺略不可勝計。

translations.literal: He advanced and took Qizhou; killings and plunder before and after were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to take Qizhou; slaughter and looting along the way were beyond count.

sentences.zh: 獲宋宗室男女七十餘口，獻之，師還。

translations.literal: More than seventy male and female members of the Song imperial clan were captured and presented; the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: More than seventy Song imperial clansmen, men and women, were captured and sent to court before the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 安貞每獲宋壯士，輒釋不殺，無慮數萬，因用其策，輒有功。

translations.literal: Whenever Anzhen captured sturdy Song men he released them without killing; they numbered in the tens of thousands without exaggeration, and by using their counsel he repeatedly achieved success.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Anzhen took able Song fighting men he spared them—tens of thousands in all—and their counsel repeatedly won him battles.

sentences.zh: 宣宗謂宰臣曰：「阿海將略善固矣，此輩得無思歸乎？

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong said to the chief ministers: "Ahai's generalship is indeed skilled—but will these men not yearn to return home?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong told his chief ministers, "Ahai's generalship is sound enough, but will these men not long for home?

sentences.zh: 南京密邇宋境，此輩既不可盡殺，安所置之？

translations.literal: Nanjing lies close to the Song border; since these men cannot all be killed, where are they to be placed?
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing lies hard against Song territory; we cannot kill them all—where should they go?

sentences.zh: 朕欲驅之境上，遣之歸如何？」

translations.literal: I wish to drive them to the frontier and send them back—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Suppose I drive them to the border and send them back to Song—what say you?"

sentences.zh: 宰臣不對。

translations.literal: The chief ministers did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers made no answer.

sentences.zh: 六月甲寅朔，尚書省奏安貞謀叛。

translations.literal: On jiayin, the first day of the sixth month, the Masters of Writing memorialized that Anzhen plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth month's first day, jiayin, the Masters of Writing Bureau reported that Anzhen was plotting rebellion.

sentences.zh: 宣宗謂平章政事英王守純曰：「朕觀此奏，皆飾詞不實，其令覆案之。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong said to Grand Councillor Prince Ying Shouchun: "I see in this memorial only embellished words, not facts—order a reinvestigation."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Grand Councillor Prince Ying Shouchun, "This memorial looks like ornament, not fact—reinvestigate it."

sentences.zh: 戊寅，並其二子殺之，以祖忠義、父揆有大功，免兄弟緣坐。

translations.literal: On wuyin he and his two sons were executed together; because his grandfather Zhongyi and his father Kui had great merit, his brothers were spared guilt by association.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin he and his two sons were executed; because his grandfather Zhongyi and father Kui had rendered great service, his brothers were spared collective punishment.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「銀青榮祿大夫、左副元帥兼樞密副使、駙馬都尉僕散阿海，早藉世姻，浸馳仕軌，屬當軍旅之事，益厚朝廷之恩，爰自帥籓，擢居樞府。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Silver-Green Glory Grandee, Left Deputy Marshal concurrent Vice Director of the Privy Council and Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant Pusan Ahai, early benefited from a hereditary marriage alliance and gradually advanced on the official track; when military affairs arose the court's favor toward him grew thicker; from commanding a frontier he was raised to the privy council.
translations.idiomatic: The edict read: "Silver-Green Glory Grandee, left deputy marshal, vice director of the privy council, and imperial son-in-law commandant Pusan Ahai rose early through a marriage alliance with the throne, advanced steadily in office, and when war came enjoyed ever thicker favor—from frontier command to the privy council.

sentences.zh: 頃者南伐，時乃奏言，是俾行鱗介之誅，而盡露梟獍之狀。

translations.literal: Recently on the southern campaign he then memorialized, which led to carrying out punishment on the scale-armored foe and fully revealing his owlish-vulture nature.
translations.idiomatic: On the recent southern campaign he memorialized in ways that sent us to punish the scaly foe—and fully exposed his treacherous heart.

sentences.zh: 二城雖得，多罪稔彰，念勝負之靡常，肯刑章之輕用。

translations.literal: Though two cities were taken, his many crimes had long been manifest; mindful that victory and defeat are inconstant, We were willing to use the penal code lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Two cities fell, yet his crimes had piled up; remembering how fortune shifts in war, We were slow to invoke the full penalty.

sentences.zh: 始自畫因糧之計，乃更嚴橫斂之期，督促計司，凋弊民力，信其私意，或失防秋。

translations.literal: Beginning with his scheme to provision armies from local grain, he then set a stricter period for exorbitant levies, urged the revenue offices, and drained the people's strength; trusting his private wishes, he sometimes neglected autumn defense.
translations.idiomatic: He began with schemes to levy grain for the armies, then tightened exactions, harried the revenue offices, and exhausted the people; indulging private designs, he even neglected autumn defenses.

sentences.zh: 顧利害之實深，尚優容而弗問。

translations.literal: Though the stakes of gain and harm were truly grave, We still treated him leniently and did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Though the stakes were grave, We still forbear and did not press him.

sentences.zh: 頃因近侍，悉露奸謀，蓋虞前後罪之上聞，乃以金玉帶而夜獻。

translations.literal: Recently through a close attendant he fully revealed his treacherous plot; fearing that his past and present crimes would reach Our ears, he presented a belt of gold and jade by night.
translations.idiomatic: Lately, through a palace attendant, his whole treason came to light; fearing his crimes would reach Us, he offered a gold-and-jade belt by night.

sentences.zh: 審事情之詭秘，命信臣而鞫推，迨致款詞，乃詳實狀。

translations.literal: Examining how secret and strange the affair was, We ordered a trusted minister to interrogate and investigate; when a full confession was obtained, the true circumstances were detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the affair too secret to trust, We sent a loyal minister to interrogate him; when he confessed, the full truth emerged.

sentences.zh: 自以積愆之著，必非公憲所容，欲結近臣之歡心，俾伺內庭之指意，如釁端之少露，得先事而易圖。

translations.literal: He himself believed his accumulated offenses were conspicuous and would surely not be tolerated by public law; he wished to win the favor of close ministers and have them watch the inner court's intentions—if the slightest sign of trouble appeared, he could act first and plot more easily.
translations.idiomatic: He knew his crimes could not stand before the law, courted palace favorites to spy on inner-court intent, and meant to strike at the first sign of trouble.

sentences.zh: 因其方握兵權，得以謀危廟祝願祏，事或不濟，計即外奔。

translations.literal: Because he then held military power, he was able to plot endangering the ancestral temple and the spirit tablets; if the affair did not succeed, his plan was at once to flee abroad.
translations.idiomatic: While he still held the armies he plotted against the ancestral temple; if the plot failed, he would flee beyond the border.

sentences.zh: 前日之俘，隨時誅戮，獨于宋族，曲活全門，示其悖德于敵仇，豫冀全身而納用。」

translations.literal: Captives of other days were put to death as occasion arose; only toward the Song clan did he bend rules to spare whole households, displaying his perverse loyalty to the enemy and hoping beforehand to save himself and be employed again."
translations.idiomatic: Other captives he killed as he pleased, but Song clansmen he spared whole households—showing his perverse loyalty to the enemy and hoping to save himself and win reinstatement."

sentences.zh: 初，安貞破蘄州，獲宋宗室不殺而獻之，遂以為罪。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Anzhen took Qizhou he captured Song imperial clansmen but did not kill them and presented them to court—this became the charge against him.
translations.idiomatic: The charge stemmed from his capture of Qizhou: he had taken Song imperial clansmen alive and sent them to court instead of killing them.

sentences.zh: 安貞憂讒，以賄近侍局，乃以質成其誣。

translations.literal: Anzhen, fearing slander, bribed the Palace Attendants Bureau, and thus material evidence confirmed the false accusation.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing slander, he bribed the palace attendants bureau—and those bribes became the "proof" of treason.

sentences.zh: 安貞典兵征伐，嘗曰：「三世為將，道家所忌。」

translations.literal: Anzhen commanded armies on campaign and once said, "Three generations as generals—this is what the Daoists warn against."
translations.idiomatic: Anzhen, who led armies in the field, once said, "Three generations of generals in one family—that is what Daoist teaching warns against."

sentences.zh: 自忠議、揆至安貞，凡三世大將焉。

translations.literal: From Zhongyi and Kui down to Anzhen, there were indeed three generations of great generals.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhongyi and Kui to Anzhen, the family had produced great generals for three generations.

sentences.zh: 初，安貞破蘄州，所得金帛，分給將士。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Anzhen took Qizhou, the gold and silks obtained were distributed among the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When he took Qizhou, the gold and silks he seized were shared among his troops.

sentences.zh: 南京都轉運使行六部事李特立，金安軍節度副使紇石烈蒲剌都、大名路總管判官銀術可因而欺隱。

translations.literal: Li Teli of Nanjing, Director of Transport acting for the Six Ministries, Hesilie Puladu, deputy military commissioner of Jin'an Army, and Yinshuke, judge under the Daming Circuit intendant, took advantage of this to conceal and embezzle.
translations.idiomatic: Li Teli, Nanjing transport director acting for the six ministries, Hesilie Puladu of Jin'an army, and Yinshuke, judge under the Daming intendant, used the occasion to embezzle.

sentences.zh: 事覺，特立當死、蒲剌都、銀術可當杖一百除名。

translations.literal: When the affair came to light, Teli was liable to death, Puladu and Yinshuke to one hundred strokes of the rod and dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: When exposed, Teli faced death, Puladu and Yinshuke a hundred strokes and dismissal.

sentences.zh: 詔薄其罪，特立奪三官、降三等，蒲剌都、銀術可奪兩官、降二等雲。

translations.literal: An edict lightened their punishments: Teli lost three ranks and was demoted three grades; Puladu and Yinshuke lost two ranks and were demoted two grades, and so forth.
translations.idiomatic: The throne lightened the sentences: Teli lost three ranks and three grades; Puladu and Yinshuke two ranks and two grades.

sentences.zh: 田琢，字器之，蔚州定安人。

translations.literal: Tian Zhuo, courtesy name Qizhi, was a native of Ding'an in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Zhuo, courtesy name Qizhi, came from Ding'an in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 中明昌五年進士，調甯邊、茌平主簿，潞州觀察判官，中都商稅副使。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Mingchang, was assigned as registrar of Ningbian and Chiping, observation judge of Luzhou, and deputy commissioner of metropolitan commercial tax.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in Mingchang year five, then served as registrar in Ningbian and Chiping, observation judge in Luzhou, and deputy metropolitan tax commissioner.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，起複懷安令，補尚書省令史。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he observed mourning, was recalled from mourning as magistrate of Huai'an, and was appointed a clerk of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he mourned, was recalled as magistrate of Huai'an, and joined the Masters of Writing as a clerk.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，中都被圍，琢請由間道往山西招集義勇，以為宣差兵馬提控、同知忠順軍節度使事，經略山西。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou, when the central capital was besieged, Zhuo requested to go by a secret route to Shanxi to gather righteous volunteers; he was made Commissioner Army Commander and Acting Military Commissioner of Zhongshun Army to oversee Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou year two, with the central capital besieged, Zhuo asked to slip through by a side route into Shanxi to raise volunteers; he was named commissioner army commander and acting Zhongshun army commissioner to oversee Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 琢與弘州刺史魏用有隙，琢自飛狐還蔚州，用伏甲于路，將邀而殺之。

translations.literal: Zhuo had a feud with Wei Yong, prefect of Hongzhou; Zhuo returned from Feihu to Weizhou, and Yong set ambush troops on the road intending to intercept and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo feuded with Hongzhou prefect Wei Yong; returning from Feihu to Weizhou, Zhuo found Yong had laid an ambush to kill him on the road.

sentences.zh: 琢知其謀，自別道入定安。

translations.literal: Zhuo learned of the plot and entered Ding'an by another route.
translations.idiomatic: Forewarned, Zhuo reached Ding'an by another road.

sentences.zh: 用入蔚州，殺觀察判官李宜，錄事判官馬士成、永興縣令張福，劫府庫倉稟，以兵攻琢于定安。

translations.literal: Yong entered Weizhou, killed observation judge Li Yi, registrar judge Ma Shicheng, and Yongxing magistrate Zhang Fu, plundered the prefectural treasury and granaries, and attacked Zhuo at Ding'an with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yong seized Weizhou, killed judge Li Yi, registrar Ma Shicheng, and Yongxing magistrate Zhang Fu, looted treasury and granaries, and marched on Zhuo at Ding'an.

sentences.zh: 琢與戰，敗之。

translations.literal: Zhuo fought him and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo met him in battle and won.

sentences.zh: 用脫身走，易州刺史蒲察縛送中都元帥府殺之。

translations.literal: Yong escaped; Pucha, prefect of Yizhou, bound him and sent him to the Central Capital Marshalate, where he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yong fled; Yizhou prefect Pucha captured him and sent him to the central marshalate for execution.

sentences.zh: 是時，勸農副使侯摯提控紫荊等關隘，朝廷聞蔚州亂，欲以摯就代琢守蔚州，令軍中推可為管押者，即以魏用金牌佩之，以安其眾。

translations.literal: At that time Agriculture Vice Commissioner Hou Zhi commanded the Zijing and other passes; when the court heard of the disorder in Weizhou it wished to send Zhi to replace Zhuo in guarding Weizhou, have the army choose someone fit to command, and give that person Wei Yong's gold tally to wear and calm the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Agriculture vice commissioner Hou Zhi then held the Zijing passes; hearing of the Weizhou revolt, court meant to send Zhi to replace Zhuo, let the troops pick a commander, and give him Wei Yong's gold tally to steady the ranks.

sentences.zh: 丞相承暉奏：「田琢實得軍民心，諳練山西利害，魏用將士本無勞效，以用弄兵死禍，遽爾任用，恐開幸門。」

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Chenghui memorialized: "Tian Zhuo truly has the hearts of army and people and knows the advantages and dangers of Shanxi; Wei Yong's officers and soldiers had no merit—because Yong raised troops he met a deadly fate; to employ someone so hastily now may open a door to favoritism."
translations.idiomatic: Chief councillor Chenghui wrote: "Tian Zhuo truly holds army and people and knows Shanxi's terrain; Wei Yong's men earned nothing—Yong died for mutiny. To rush a replacement may open the door to court favoritism."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The edict agreed.

sentences.zh: 琢至蔚州，誅與用同惡數人。

translations.literal: Zhuo reached Weizhou and executed several men who shared Yong's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo reached Weizhou and executed several of Yong's accomplices.

sentences.zh: 募兵旬日，得二萬人。

translations.literal: In ten days of recruiting he obtained twenty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he raised twenty thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 十月，琢兵敗，僅以身免。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Zhuo's army was defeated and he barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month his army was beaten and he barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 招集散亡，得三萬餘，入中山界屯駐，而遣沈思忠招集西京蕩析百姓，得萬餘人，皆願徙河南。

translations.literal: He gathered the scattered and fugitive, obtaining more than thirty thousand, and encamped within Zhongshan territory; he sent Shen Sizhong to gather the uprooted commoners of the Western Capital, obtaining more than ten thousand, all wishing to move south to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He rallied over thirty thousand stragglers and camped in Zhongshan; Shen Sizhong gathered more than ten thousand displaced Western Capital people who all wished to move to Henan.

sentences.zh: 琢上書：「此輩與河南鎮防，往往鄉舊，若令南渡，擇壯健為兵，自然和協，且可以招集其餘也。」

translations.literal: Zhuo memorialized: "These people and the garrison troops in Henan are often fellow townsmen; if they are made to cross south, and the sturdy are chosen as soldiers, they will naturally harmonize, and the rest can also be gathered in."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo wrote: "These people often have kin among the Henan garrisons; if we move them south and draft the able-bodied, they will settle in naturally and draw others after them."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 加沈思忠同知深州軍州事。

translations.literal: Shen Sizhong was made Acting Administrator of Shenzhou prefecture and army.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Sizhong was made acting administrator of Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 琢複遣沈思忠、宮楫招弘州、蔚州百姓，得五萬餘人，可充軍者萬五千人，分屯蔚州諸隘，皆願得沈思忠為將。

translations.literal: Zhuo again sent Shen Sizhong and Gong Ji to recruit the people of Hongzhou and Weizhou, obtaining more than fifty thousand, of whom fifteen thousand could serve as soldiers; they were stationed at the various passes of Weizhou, all wishing to have Shen Sizhong as their commander.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo sent Shen Sizhong and Gong Ji to recruit Hongzhou and Weizhou—over fifty thousand people, fifteen thousand fit for service—posted at Weizhou passes, all asking for Shen Sizhong as commander.

sentences.zh: 詔加思忠順天軍節度副使，提控弘、蔚州軍馬，宮楫副之。

translations.literal: An edict promoted Sizhong to deputy military commissioner of Shuntian Army, commander of Hong and Weizhou forces, with Gong Ji as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhong was made deputy Shuntian army commissioner to command Hong and Weizhou troops, with Gong Ji as deputy.

sentences.zh: 頃之，西山諸隘皆不能守。

translations.literal: Before long all the western mountain passes could no longer be held.
translations.idiomatic: Soon every western pass was lost.

sentences.zh: 琢移軍沃州。

translations.literal: Zhuo moved his army to Wozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo shifted his army to Wozhou.

sentences.zh: 沃州刺史完顏僧家奴奏：「田琢軍二千五百人，官廩不足，發民窖粟猶不能贍。

translations.literal: Wanyan Sengjianu, prefect of Wozhou, memorialized: "Tian Zhuo's army of twenty-five hundred men—the official granaries are insufficient; even issuing the people's stored grain from cellars cannot feed them.
translations.idiomatic: Wozhou prefect Wanyan Sengjianu reported: "Zhuo's twenty-five hundred men cannot be fed from official stores—even digging out private cellar grain is not enough.

sentences.zh: 其中多女直人，均為一軍，不可複有厚薄，可令于衛、輝、大名就食。」

translations.literal: Among them are many Jurchen; they are one army together and cannot again be treated with partiality; they may be sent to Wei, Hui, and Daming to obtain food."
translations.idiomatic: Many are Jurchen in one unit—they must not be split unevenly; let them forage in Wei, Hui, and Daming."

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 加琢河北西路宣撫副使，遙授浚州防禦使，屯浚州。

translations.literal: Zhuo was made Pacification Vice Commissioner of Hebei West Circuit, remotely appointed Defense Commissioner of Xunzhou, and encamped at Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo became Hebei west circuit pacification vice commissioner, was given the remote title defense commissioner of Xunzhou, and camped there.

sentences.zh: 琢欲陂西山諸水以衛浚州。

translations.literal: Zhuo wished to dam the waters of the western mountains to protect Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo planned to dam western mountain streams to shield Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 貞祐三年十一月，河北行省侯摯入見，奏：「河北兵食少，請令琢汰遣老弱，就食歸德。」

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Zhenyou, Hebei Branch Secretariat Hou Zhi came to audience and memorialized: "Hebei troops have little food; please order Zhuo to weed out and send away the old and weak to obtain food at Guide."
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou year three, eleventh month, Hebei branch secretary Hou Zhi memorialized: "Hebei troops lack food—order Zhuo to discharge the old and weak to forage at Guide."

sentences.zh: 琢奏：「此輩嶺外失業，父子兄弟合為一軍，若離而分之，定生他變，乞以全軍南渡，或徙衛州防河。」

translations.literal: Zhuo memorialized: "These people lost their livelihoods beyond the passes; fathers, sons, and brothers form one army together—if separated and divided, other troubles will surely arise; I beg that the whole army cross south, or be moved to Weizhou to guard the river."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo replied: "These refugees beyond the passes fight as family units—split them and they will mutiny; move the whole army south or post it at Weizhou on the river."

sentences.zh: 詔盡徙屯陝。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the entire force moved and encamped in Shaan.
translations.idiomatic: The edict ordered the entire force relocated to Shaan.

sentences.zh: 琢複奏：「臣幸徙安地，然浚乃河北要郡，今見糧可支數月，乞俟來春乃行。」

translations.literal: Zhuo again memorialized: "Your servant is fortunate to move to a secure region, yet Xun is a key prefecture of Hebei; grain on hand can last several months—I beg to wait until next spring before departing."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo wrote again: "I am glad to move to safer ground, but Xun is a key Hebei prefecture and has grain for months—I ask to wait until spring."

sentences.zh: 數日，琢複奏：「浚不可守，惟當遷之。」

translations.literal: A few days later Zhuo again memorialized: "Xun cannot be defended and must be abandoned."
translations.idiomatic: Days later he wrote: "Xun cannot be held—we must leave."

sentences.zh: 宰臣劾琢前後奏陳不一，請逮鞫問。

translations.literal: The chief ministers impeached Zhuo for inconsistent memorials before and after and requested that he be arrested and interrogated.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers accused him of contradicting himself and asked to arrest and question him.

sentences.zh: 宣宗不許。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 琢至陝，上書曰：「河北失業之民僑居河南、陝西，蓋不可以數計。

translations.literal: When Zhuo reached Shaan he memorialized: "The displaced people of Hebei who sojourn in Henan and Shaanxi cannot be counted.
translations.idiomatic: At Shaan, Zhuo wrote: "Hebei refugees in Henan and Shaanxi are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 百司用度，三軍調發，一人耕之，百人食之，其能贍乎？

translations.literal: The expenses of the hundred offices, the levies of the three armies—one man tills while a hundred eat; how can this be sustained?
translations.idiomatic: Court offices and three armies consume—one farmer feeds a hundred mouths. How can that last?

sentences.zh: 春種不廣，收成失望，軍民俱困，實系安危。

translations.literal: Spring planting is not extensive; harvests fall short of hope; army and people alike are distressed—this truly bears on safety and peril.
translations.idiomatic: Spring planting is thin, harvests disappoint, army and people suffer—this touches the state's survival.

sentences.zh: 臣聞古之名將，雖在征行，必須屯田，趙充國、諸葛亮是也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that famous generals of old, even on campaign, had to practice garrison farming—Zhao Chongguo and Zhuge Liang were such men.
translations.idiomatic: Famous generals—even on campaign—farmed garrison fields: Zhao Chongguo and Zhuge Liang did so.

sentences.zh: 古之良吏，必課農桑以足民，黃霸、虞詡是也。

translations.literal: Good officials of old surely promoted agriculture and sericulture to fill the people's needs—Huang Ba and Yu Xu were such men.
translations.idiomatic: Good magistrates promoted farming and sericulture to feed the people—Huang Ba and Yu Xu did.

sentences.zh: 方今曠土多，遊民眾，乞明敕有司，無蹈虛文，嚴升降之法，選能吏勸課，公私皆得耕墾。

translations.literal: Today idle land is abundant and vagrant people numerous; I beg a clear edict to the offices not to follow empty forms, to enforce strict promotion and demotion, to choose capable officials to encourage cultivation, so that public and private alike may till and open land.
translations.idiomatic: Idle land abounds and wanderers swarm; order officials to drop empty forms, enforce merit rules, send able magistrates to promote farming, and let public and private fields be opened.

sentences.zh: 富者備牛出種，貧者傭力服勤。

translations.literal: The rich should ready oxen and provide seed; the poor should hire out their labor and work diligently.
translations.idiomatic: Let the rich supply oxen and seed; let the poor hire out as laborers.

sentences.zh: 若又不足，則教之區種，期於盡辟而後已。

translations.literal: If that is still insufficient, then teach them pit-planting, aiming to open all land before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: If that fails, teach pit-planting until every plot is cleared.

sentences.zh: 官司圉牧，勢家兼併，亦籍其數而授之農民，寬其負算，省其徭役，使盡力南畝，則蓄積歲增，家給人足，富國強兵之道也。」

translations.literal: Government pastures and powerful families' encroachments should also be registered by number and granted to farmers; lighten their tax burdens, reduce their corvée, and let them exert themselves in the southern fields—then stores will grow year by year, households will be provided for and people satisfied; this is the way to enrich the state and strengthen the army."
translations.idiomatic: Register government pastures and powerful estates, assign them to farmers, lighten taxes and corvée, and let men work the fields—stores will grow, households prosper, and the state grow strong."

sentences.zh: 宣宗深然之。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 是月，棣州裨將張聚殺防禦使斜卯重興，遂據棣州，襲濱州，其眾數千人。

translations.literal: That month Zhang Ju, adjutant of Dizhou, killed Defense Commissioner Xieyao Chongxing, then seized Dizhou and raided Binzhou; his followers numbered several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: That month Dizhou adjutant Zhang Ju killed defense commissioner Xieyao Chongxing, seized Dizhou, raided Binzhou, and mustered several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 琢遣提控紇石烈醜漢會兵討之。

translations.literal: Zhuo sent Commander Hesilie Chouhan to join forces and suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo sent commander Hesilie Chouhan with allied troops against him.

sentences.zh: 聚棄濱專保棣州。

translations.literal: Ju abandoned Bin and held only Dizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ju gave up Binzhou and held only Dizhou.

sentences.zh: 諸軍趣棣，聚出戰，敗之，斬首百級，生擒偽都統王仙等十三人。

translations.literal: The armies hurried to Di; Ju came out to fight and was defeated; a hundred heads were taken and thirteen men including the false commander-in-chief Wang Xian were captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: Government forces closed on Di; Ju met them and lost a hundred heads, with thirteen captives including the rebel commander Wang Xian.

sentences.zh: 餘眾奔潰，追及於別寨，攻拔之，聚僅以身免。

translations.literal: The remainder fled in rout; pursued to another camp, it was stormed and taken; Ju barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Survivors fled; pursuers stormed a second camp; Ju alone escaped.

sentences.zh: 遂複二州。

translations.literal: The two prefectures were thus recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Both prefectures were recovered.

sentences.zh: 李全據安丘，琢遣總領提控王政、王庭玉討之。

translations.literal: Li Quan held Anqiu; Zhuo sent Overall Commanders Wang Zheng and Wang Tingyu to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Quan held Anqiu; Zhuo sent overall commanders Wang Zheng and Wang Tingyu against him.

sentences.zh: 宣差提控、太府少監伯德玩率政兵攻安丘，敗焉，提控王顯死之。

translations.literal: Commissioner Commander and Vice Director of the Grand Treasury Bode Wan led Zheng's troops to attack Anqiu, was defeated, and Commander Wang Xian died in the action.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Bode Wan of the grand treasury led Zheng's men on Anqiu, was beaten, and commander Wang Xian was killed.

sentences.zh: 琢奏：「伯德玩本相視山東山堌水寨，未嘗遍行，獨留密州，輒為此舉，乞治其罪。」

translations.literal: Zhuo memorialized: "Bode Wan was originally to survey Shandong's mountain stockades and river camps but never traveled everywhere—he stayed only in Mizhou and rashly made this move; I beg that he be punished."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo wrote: "Bode Wan was to survey Shandong stockades but never toured—he stayed in Mizhou and launched this attack on his own; punish him."

sentences.zh: 詔遣官鞫玩，會赦而止。

translations.literal: An edict sent officials to try Wan, but an amnesty arrived and the case stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were sent to try him, but an amnesty halted the case.

sentences.zh: 既而昌樂縣令術虎桓都、臨朐縣令兀顏吾丁、福山縣令烏林答石家奴、壽光縣巡檢紇石烈醜漢破李全於日照縣，琢承制各遷官一階，進職一等，詔許之。

translations.literal: Soon after, Changyue magistrate Shuohu Huandu, Linqu magistrate Wanyan Wuding, Fushan magistrate Wulindaxi Shijianu, and Shouguang inspector Hesilie Chouhan defeated Li Quan at Rizhao County; Zhuo by imperial commission promoted each one rank and one grade in office, and the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Later Changyue magistrate Shuohu Huandu, Linqu magistrate Wanyan Wuding, Fushan magistrate Wulindaxi Shijianu, and Shouguang inspector Hesilie Chouhan beat Li Quan at Rizhao; Zhuo promoted each one rank and grade, and court approved.

sentences.zh: 三年，沂州注子堌王公喜構宋兵據沂州，防禦使徒單福定徒跣脫走，百姓潰散。

translations.literal: In the third year Wang Gongxi of Zhuzi Stockade in Yizhou colluded with Song troops to seize Yizhou; Defense Commissioner Tushan Fuding fled barefoot, and the people scattered.
translations.idiomatic: In year three Wang Gongxi of Yizhou's Zhuzi stockade brought in Song troops; defense commissioner Tushan Fuding fled barefoot and the populace broke.

sentences.zh: 琢奏：「去歲顧王二嘗據沂州，邳州總領提控納合六哥前為同知沂州防禦事，招集餘眾攻取之，百姓歸心。

translations.literal: Zhuo memorialized: "Last year Gu Wang'er once held Yizhou; Pizhou Overall Commander Nahe Liuge had formerly been Acting Defense Commissioner of Yizhou, gathered the remaining troops and retook it, and the people gave him their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo wrote: "Last year Gu Wang'er held Yizhou; Pizhou commander Nahe Liuge, once acting Yizhou defense commissioner, rallied remnants and retook it—the people trust him.

sentences.zh: 可用六哥取沂州，今方在行省侯摯麾下，乞發還，取便道進討。」

translations.literal: Liuge can be used to retake Yizhou; he is now under Branch Secretary Hou Zhi—I beg that he be sent back by a convenient route to advance and attack."
translations.idiomatic: Send Liuge back from Hou Zhi's staff by the quickest route to retake Yizhou."

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: Approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 既而莒州提控燕寧複沂州，王公喜複保注子堌。

translations.literal: Soon after Juzhou Commander Yan Ning recovered Yizhou, and Wang Gongxi again held Zhuzi Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yan Ning of Juzhou retook Yizhou; Wang Gongxi fell back to Zhuzi stockade.

sentences.zh: 琢奏：「沂州須知兵者守之。

translations.literal: Zhuo memorialized: "Yizhou must be guarded by one who knows warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo wrote: "Yizhou needs a soldier-governor.

sentences.zh: 徒單福定已衰老，納合六哥善治兵，識沂形勢。」

translations.literal: Tushan Fuding is already aged; Nahe Liuge is skilled at managing troops and knows Yi's terrain."
translations.idiomatic: Tushan Fuding is old; Nahe Liuge knows how to command and knows Yi's ground."

sentences.zh: 詔福定專治州事，以六哥為沂州總領。

translations.literal: An edict had Fuding administer only civil prefectural affairs and made Liuge overall commander of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fuding was left to civil administration; Liuge became overall Yizhou commander.

sentences.zh: 琢奏：「濰州刺史致仕獨吉世顯能招集猛安餘眾及義軍，卻李全，保濰州。

translations.literal: Zhuo memorialized: "Retired Weizhou Prefect Duji Shixian can gather the remaining men of the meng'an and the righteous armies, repel Li Quan, and preserve Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo praised retired Weizhou prefect Duji Shixian for rallying meng'an remnants and militia, driving off Li Quan, and holding Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 六哥破灰山堌，沂境以安。

translations.literal: Liuge broke Huishan Stockade and the Yi region was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Liuge stormed Huishan stockade and secured Yi territory.

sentences.zh: 守兗州觀察判官梁昱嘗攝淄州刺史，率軍民力田，征科有度，饋餉不乏，保全淄州，土賊不敢發。

translations.literal: Liang Yu, observation judge defending Yanzhou, once acted as prefect of Zizhou; he led army and people in field labor, levied taxes with measure, supplies never failed, preserved Zizhou, and local bandits dared not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou judge Liang Yu, once acting Zi prefect, led troops and civilians in farming, taxed fairly, kept supplies flowing, held Zi, and kept local bandits down.

sentences.zh: 前猗氏主簿張亞夫嘗權行部官，主餉密州，委曲購得糧二萬斛，兵儲乃足，行至高密，征他州兵拒李全。」

translations.literal: Former Yishi registrar Zhang Yafu once acted as a touring department official, managed provisions for Mizhou, and by every means purchased twenty thousand hu of grain so that army stores were full; marching to Gaomi he levied troops from other prefectures to resist Li Quan."
translations.idiomatic: Former Yishi registrar Zhang Yafu once ran supply for Mizhou, bought twenty thousand hu of grain by every means, filled the magazines, marched to Gaomi, and raised troops from other prefectures against Li Quan."

sentences.zh: 詔世顯升職從四品，遙授同知海州事。

translations.literal: An edict promoted Shixian in rank to fourth grade, junior, and remotely appointed him Acting Administrator of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shixian was raised to junior fourth grade and given the remote post acting administrator of Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 六哥遷一官，升一等，充沂州宣差都提控。

translations.literal: Liuge was transferred one rank, promoted one grade, and made Commissioner Overall Commander of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liuge gained one rank and grade and became Yizhou commissioner overall commander.

sentences.zh: 梁昱遷一官，同知淄州事。

translations.literal: Liang Yu was transferred one rank and made Acting Administrator of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yu gained one rank and became acting administrator of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 張亞夫遷兩官，密州觀察判官。

translations.literal: Zhang Yafu was transferred two ranks and made observation judge of Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yafu gained two ranks and became Mizhou observation judge.

sentences.zh: 初，張林本益都府卒，有複立府事之功，遂為治中，而兇險不逞，恥出琢下。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhang Lin had been a soldier of the Yidu prefecture office; he had merit in restoring the prefecture and thus became Administrator, but he was fierce and unbridled and ashamed to stand below Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lin, once a Yidu office soldier, had helped restore the prefecture and became administrator, but he was violent and resented serving under Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 琢在山東徵求過當，頗失眾心，林欲因眾以去琢，未有間也。

translations.literal: Zhuo's exactions in Shandong were excessive and he lost much popular support; Lin wished to use the masses to remove Zhuo but had no opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo's levies in Shandong were harsh and cost him support; Lin wanted a popular rising against him but found no opening.

sentences.zh: 會于海、牟佐據萊州，琢遣林分兵討之。

translations.literal: When Yu Hai and Mou Zuo seized Laizhou, Zhuo sent Lin with divided troops to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Hai and Mou Zuo took Laizhou, Zhuo sent Lin with a detachment against them.

sentences.zh: 林既得兵，伺琢出，即率眾噪入府中。

translations.literal: Once Lin had troops, he watched for Zhuo to go out, then led a clamoring mob into the government house.
translations.idiomatic: Once armed, Lin waited until Zhuo left, then stormed the yamen with a mob.

sentences.zh: 琢倉猝入營，領兵與林戰，不勝，欲就外縣兵，且戰且行。

translations.literal: Zhuo hastily entered camp, led troops to fight Lin, was defeated, and intended to join troops from outer counties, fighting as he went.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo rushed to camp, fought Lin, lost, and retreated fighting toward county garrisons.

sentences.zh: 至章丘，兵變，求救於鄰道，不時至。

translations.literal: At Zhangqiu his troops mutinied; he sought rescue from neighboring circuits but help did not arrive in time.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhangqiu his men mutinied; neighboring circuits were summoned but help came too late.

sentences.zh: 東平行省蒙古綱以狀聞。

translations.literal: Meng Gugang of the Dongping Branch Secretariat reported the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Dongping branch secretary Meng Gugang reported the affair.

sentences.zh: 宣宗度不能制林，而欲馴致之，乃遣人召琢還。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong judged that Lin could not be controlled and wished to bring him to heel gradually, and so sent men to recall Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged Lin uncontrollable and hoped to tame him gradually, and recalled Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 行至壽張，疽發背卒。

translations.literal: When he reached Shouzhang a carbuncle broke out on his back and he died.
translations.idiomatic: At Shouzhang a back abscess killed him.

sentences.zh: 完顏弼

translations.literal: Wanyan Bi
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Bi

sentences.zh: 完顏弼，本名達吉不，蓋州猛安人。

translations.literal: Wanyan Bi, original name Dajibu, was a man of the Gaizhou meng'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Bi, original name Dajibu, came from the Gaizhou meng'an.

sentences.zh: 充護衛，轉十人長。

translations.literal: He served as a guardsman and was transferred to leader of ten.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the guards and became a decurion.

sentences.zh: 從丞相襄戍邊，功最，除同知德州防禦使事，武衛軍鈐轄，轉宿直將軍、深州刺史。

translations.literal: Following Chancellor Xiang on frontier garrison duty, his merit was foremost; he was appointed Acting Defense Commissioner of Dezhou, seal-holder of the Martial Guard Army, then transferred to Palace Duty General and prefect of Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On frontier service under Chancellor Xiang his merit ranked first; he became acting Dezhou defense commissioner, Martial Guard seal-holder, then palace duty general and Shenzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 泰和六年，從左副元帥完顏匡攻襄陽，破雷太尉兵，積功加平南蕩江將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe he followed Left Deputy Marshal Wanyan Kuang in attacking Xiangyang, defeated Grand Marshal Lei's troops, and for accumulated merit was given the rank Pacify-the-South Suppress-the-River General.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe year six he followed left deputy marshal Wanyan Kuang against Xiangyang, broke Grand Marshal Lei's force, and was made Pacify-the-South Suppress-the-River General.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起複。

translations.literal: Upon his mother's death he observed mourning, then was recalled from mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned his mother, then was recalled to duty.

sentences.zh: 八年，除南京副留守、壽州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was made Vice Protector of Nanjing and Defense Commissioner of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight he became Nanjing vice protector and Shouzhou defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 大安二年，入為武衛軍副都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Da'an he entered the capital as Vice Commander of the Martial Guard Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Da'an year two he entered court as vice commander of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 三年，以本官領兵駐宣德。

translations.literal: In the third year, in his existing office, he led troops stationed at Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he led troops to garrison Xuande in the same post.

sentences.zh: 會河之敗，弼被創，馬中流矢，押軍千戶夾谷王家奴以馬授弼，遂得免。

translations.literal: At the defeat on the river Bi was wounded; his horse was struck by an arrow; Escort Army chiliarch Jiagu Wangjianu gave Bi his horse, and thus he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: At the river defeat Bi was wounded and his horse shot; escort chiliarch Jiagu Wangjianu gave him his mount and he escaped.

sentences.zh: 遷右副都點檢。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Deputy Chief Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He was made right deputy chief inspector.

sentences.zh: 貞祐初，宣宗驛召弼赴中都，是時雲內已受兵，弼善馬槊，與數騎突出，由太原出澤、潞，將從清、滄赴闕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyou Emperor Xuanzong summoned Bi by post-station relay to the central capital; Yunnei was already under attack; Bi was skilled with the horse lance and broke out with several horsemen, went out from Taiyuan through Ze and Lu, and intended to reach court by way of Qing and Cang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenyou the emperor summoned Bi to the capital; Yunnei was already under attack. Skilled with the cavalry lance, Bi broke out with a few riders, passed through Taiyuan and Ze-Lu, and aimed to reach court via Qing and Cang.

sentences.zh: 會有詔除定武軍節度使，尋為元帥左都監，駐真定。

translations.literal: An edict then appointed him Military Commissioner of Dingwu Army; soon he became Left Overseer of the Marshalate and was stationed at Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named him Dingwu army commissioner; soon he became left marshal overseer at Zhending.

sentences.zh: 弼奏：「賞罰所以勸善懲惡，有功必賞，有罪必罰，而後人可使、兵可強。

translations.literal: Bi memorialized: "Rewards and punishments exist to encourage good and chastise evil; merit must be rewarded and guilt punished—only then can men be employed and armies strengthened.
translations.idiomatic: Bi wrote: "Rewards and punishments encourage virtue and restrain evil; merit must be rewarded and crime punished—only then can men be led and armies strengthened.

sentences.zh: 今外兵日增，軍無鬥志。

translations.literal: Now external enemies increase daily and the army lacks fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy pressure grows daily while our troops lack fight.

sentences.zh: 亦有逃歸而以戰潰自陳者，有司從而存恤之，見聞習熟，相效成風。」

translations.literal: Some flee back and report defeat in battle, yet the offices comfort and support them; what is seen and heard becomes familiar and imitated until it becomes custom."
translations.idiomatic: Men flee and claim defeat, yet officials comfort them—others see it and copy the habit."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「村寨城邑，兵退之後，有心力勇敢可使者，乞招用之。」

translations.literal: He also said: "In villages, stockades, and towns, after troops withdraw, those with strength of mind and courage fit for use—I beg that they be recruited."
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to recruit brave men from villages and towns after armies withdraw."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「河朔郡縣，皆以拘文不相應救，由此殘破。

translations.literal: He also said: "Hebei prefectures and districts all fail to rescue one another because of bureaucratic formalities, and thus lie in ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei counties fail to aid each other because of red tape—that is why the region is ruined.

sentences.zh: 乞敕州府，凡有告急徵兵，即須赴救，違者坐之。」

translations.literal: I beg an edict to prefectures and districts: whenever urgent calls summon troops, they must go to the rescue; violators are to be punished."
translations.idiomatic: Order every prefecture: when another calls for help, march at once—or face punishment."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「河北軍器，乞權宜弛禁，仍令團結堡寨以備外兵。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Hebei weapons—I beg that prohibitions be relaxed as expedient, and that fortified stockades be organized to guard against external troops."
translations.idiomatic: Relax Hebei arms restrictions and organize fortified stockades against invaders."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「今雖議和，萬一輕騎複來，則吾民重困矣。

translations.literal: He also said: "Though peace is now discussed, if light cavalry should come again, our people will be doubly afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: Though we talk peace, if enemy cavalry return our people will suffer again.

sentences.zh: 願速講防禦之策。」

translations.literal: I wish that defense plans be discussed quickly."
translations.idiomatic: Let us plan defenses at once."

sentences.zh: 及勸遷都南京，阻長淮，拒大河，扼潼關以自固。

translations.literal: He also urged moving the capital to Nanjing, blocking the long Huai, holding the great river, and seizing Tong Pass to secure the state.
translations.idiomatic: He urged moving the capital to Nanjing, holding the Huai, the Yellow River, and Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 宣宗將遷汴，弼兼河北西路兵馬都總管。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to move the capital to Bian, Bi was concurrently Overall Commander of Hebei West Circuit forces.
translations.idiomatic: As the court prepared to move to Bian, Bi also commanded Hebei west circuit forces.

sentences.zh: 宣宗次真定，弼言：「皇太子不可留中都，蓋軍少則難守，軍多則難養。」

translations.literal: When the emperor halted at Zhending, Bi said, "The crown prince cannot remain in the central capital—for if troops are few it is hard to defend, and if many it is hard to supply."
translations.idiomatic: At Zhending Bi said, "The crown prince should not stay in the central capital—too few troops cannot hold it, too many cannot be fed."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「將帥以閫外為威，今生殺之權皆從中覆。」

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Generals derive authority from command beyond the capital, yet now the power of life and death is all subject to central review."
translations.idiomatic: He also said field commanders need autonomy of life and death, not constant central review."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「瑞州軍頗狡，左丞盡忠多疑，乞付他將。」

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "The Ruizhou army is rather cunning; Left Chancellor Jinzhong is overly suspicious—I beg that another general be assigned."
translations.idiomatic: He asked to replace Left Chancellor Jinzhong, who was too suspicious of the crafty Ruizhou army."

sentences.zh: 宣宗頗採用其言。

translations.literal: The emperor largely adopted his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor largely followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 大名軍變，殺蒲察阿裏，詔弼鎮撫之。

translations.literal: The Daming army mutinied and killed Pucha Ali; an edict ordered Bi to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Daming troops mutinied and killed Pucha Ali; Bi was ordered to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改陝西路統軍使、京兆兵馬都總管。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to Military Commissioner of Shaanxi Circuit and Overall Commander of Jingzhao forces.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Shaanxi military commissioner and Jingzhao overall commander.

sentences.zh: 宣撫副使烏古論兗州置秦州榷場，弼以擅置，移文問之。

translations.literal: Pacification Vice Commissioner Wugulun Yanzhou established a Qinzhou market bureau; Bi, on grounds of unauthorized action, sent a document to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification vice commissioner Wugulun of Yanzhou opened a Qinzhou trade bureau; Bi challenged the unauthorized act in writing.

sentences.zh: 兗州曰：「近日入見，許山外從宜行事，秦州自宋兵焚蕩榷場，幾一年矣，今既安帖，複宜開設，彼此獲利，歲收以十萬計。

translations.literal: Yanzhou replied: "On a recent audience I was permitted to act as expedient beyond the passes; since Song troops burned the Qinzhou market bureau it has been nearly a year; now that things are settled it should be reopened—both sides profit, with yearly receipts on the order of one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou replied: "The throne recently let me act beyond the passes as needed. Song burned the Qinzhou market a year ago; now it should reopen—both sides profit, with yearly receipts around one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 對境天水軍移文來請，如俟報可，實慮後時。」

translations.literal: The Tianshui army across the border sent a document requesting it; if we wait for approval it will truly be feared to come too late."
translations.idiomatic: The Tianshui garrison across the border has asked; waiting for approval may be too late."

sentences.zh: 弼奏其事，宰臣以兗州雖擅舉而無違失，苟利於民，專之亦可。

translations.literal: Bi memorialized the matter; chief ministers held that though Yanzhou acted on its own without violation, if it benefited the people, exclusive authority was also acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Bi reported it; ministers said Yanzhou acted alone but without harm—if it helped the people, let it stand.

sentences.zh: 宣宗曰：「朕固嘗許其從宜也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I had indeed already permitted him to act as expedient."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I had already allowed him to act as needed."

sentences.zh: 三年，改知東平府事、山東西路宣撫副使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was changed to Administrator of Dongping Prefecture and Pacification Vice Commissioner of Shandong West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he became administrator of Dongping and Shandong west circuit pacification vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是時，劉二祖餘黨孫邦佐、張汝楫保濟南勤子堌，弼遣人招之，得邦佐書雲：「我輩自軍興屢立戰功，主將見忌，陰圖陷害，竄伏山林，以至今日，實畏死耳。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Erzu's remnant partisans Sun Bangzuo and Zhang Ruji held Qinzi Stockade near Jinan; Bi sent men to recruit them and received Bangzuo's letter saying, "We have repeatedly won battle merit since the war began; our commander grew jealous and secretly plotted against us; we hid in mountains and forests until today—truly we fear death.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Erzu's followers Sun Bangzuo and Zhang Ruji held Qinzi stockade near Jinan. Bangzuo wrote back: "We won battles from the start, but our commander envied us and plotted against us—we hid in the hills because we fear death.

sentences.zh: 如蒙湔洗，便當釋險面縛，餘賊未降者保盡招之。」

translations.literal: If we receive pardon and cleansing, we will at once leave our strongholds and bind ourselves; the remaining rebels who have not submitted—I guarantee to recruit them all."
translations.idiomatic: Grant amnesty and we will surrender and bring in every rebel still at large."

sentences.zh: 弼奏：「方今多故，此賊果定，亦一事畢也。

translations.literal: Bi memorialized: "In today's many troubles, if these rebels are truly settled, that too is one affair completed.
translations.idiomatic: Bi wrote: "In these troubled times, settling this band would finish one major task.

sentences.zh: 乞明以官賞示之。」

translations.literal: I beg that official rewards be shown them clearly."
translations.idiomatic: Show them clear official rewards."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「孫邦佐果受招，各遷五官職。」

translations.literal: The edict said: "If Sun Bangzuo truly accepts recruitment, each is promoted five ranks in office."
translations.idiomatic: The edict promised five rank promotions if Sun Bangzuo submitted."

sentences.zh: 於是邦佐、汝楫皆降。

translations.literal: Thereupon Bangzuo and Ruji both surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Both men surrendered.

sentences.zh: 邦佐遙授濰州刺史，汝楫遙授淄州刺史，皆加明威將軍。

translations.literal: Bangzuo was remotely appointed prefect of Weizhou, Ruji remotely appointed prefect of Zizhou; both were given the rank Bright Authority General.
translations.idiomatic: Bangzuo received the remote title Weizhou prefect, Ruji Zizhou prefect, both as Bright Authority generals.

sentences.zh: 頃之，弼薦邦佐、汝楫改過用命，招降甚眾，稍收其兵仗，放歸田裏。

translations.literal: Before long Bi recommended that Bangzuo and Ruji, having reformed and obeyed orders, had recruited many surrenders, gradually collected their weapons, and released them to their fields.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Bi reported that both men had reformed, brought in many surrenders, surrendered arms, and returned to farming.

sentences.zh: 詔邦佐遙授同知益都府事，汝楫遙授同知東平府事，皆加懷遠大將軍。

translations.literal: An edict remotely appointed Bangzuo Acting Administrator of Yidu Prefecture and Ruji Acting Administrator of Dongping Prefecture; both were given the rank Cherish-the-Distant Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Bangzuo was made acting administrator of Yidu, Ruji of Dongping, both as Cherish-the-Distant grand generals.

sentences.zh: 梁聚寬遙授泰定軍節度副使，加宣武將軍。

translations.literal: Liang Jukuan was remotely appointed deputy military commissioner of Taiding Army and given the rank Proclaim-Martial General.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Jukuan became remote deputy Taiding army commissioner with the rank Proclaim-Martial general.

sentences.zh: 四年，弼遷宣撫使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Bi was transferred to Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In year four Bi became pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 已而汝楫複謀作亂，邦佐密告弼，弼饗汝楫，伏甲廡下，酒數行，鐘鳴伏發，殺汝楫並其黨與。

translations.literal: Soon Ruji again plotted rebellion; Bangzuo secretly informed Bi; Bi feasted Ruji with ambush troops below the side halls; after several rounds of wine, at the bell's strike the ambush rose and killed Ruji and his partisans.
translations.idiomatic: Ruji plotted again; Bangzuo warned Bi, who feasted him with hidden troops; at the bell signal they killed Ruji and his followers.

sentences.zh: 手詔褒諭，封密國公。

translations.literal: An imperial hand-edict praised him, and he was enfeoffed as Duke of Miguo.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial letter praised him and made him Duke of Miguo.

sentences.zh: 其後邦佐屢立功。

translations.literal: Afterward Bangzuo repeatedly achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: Bangzuo later won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 元光末，累官知東平府事、山東西路兵馬都總管，充宣差招撫使。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanguang, through accumulated offices he was Administrator of Dongping Prefecture and Overall Commander of Shandong West Circuit forces, serving as Commissioner Pacification Envoy.
translations.idiomatic: By late Yuanguang he was Dongping administrator, Shandong west overall commander, and commissioner pacification envoy.

sentences.zh: 弼上書曰：「山東、河北、河東數鎮僅能自守，恐長河之險有不足恃者。

translations.literal: Bi memorialized: "Several garrisons in Shandong, Hebei, and Hedong can barely hold themselves; I fear the long river's defenses may not suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Bi wrote: "Shandong, Hebei, and Hedong garrisons barely hold on—the great river may not be enough.

sentences.zh: 河南嘗招戰士，率皆遊惰市人，不閑訓練。
